text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Indonesian President Suharto, describing 1997-8 as a "political year" during which Indonesians will go to the polls, unveils budget aimed at enhancing government's pro-people image.
- Labour strikes erupt in South Korea with new ferocity as state prosecutors and management of industrial conglomerates launch offensive against union leaders.
- Two-million-barrel-per-day oil pipeline will be built across Malay peninsula from Sai Buri on east coast of southern Thailand to Alor Star on west coast of Malaysia, Chiyoda Corp says.
- 51-year-old man believed to be cigarette-smuggling syndicate chief fined record Singapore $5.3 million.
- Property subsidiary of Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry launches tender seeking partner for S$350 million commercial development on downtown site.
- Door maker Chuan Soon Huat Industrial Group will launch initial public offering.
- Indonesia intends to offer tax holidays to selected companies in strategic industries to lure them from competing countries, trade and industry minister says.
- Multi-billionaire Li Ka-shing unveils reshuffling of assets in his four major Hong Kong listed vehicles in move says will benefit all four and boost growing infrastructure business.
- Singapore Airlines looking into floating major subsidiaries such as Singapore Airport Terminal Services, SIA Engineering and SilkAir.
- Southeast and East Asian economies poised to see recovery in economic growth to 7-8 percent in 1997, economists say.
- Several fund managers restructuring Central Provident Fund approved unit trusts to bring them in line with liberalised CPF investment guidelines which came into effect on January 1.
- All 40 million placement shares of Hong Kong-based mould base maker Lung Kee Metals Holdings Ltd's initial public offer taken up.
- LC Development Ltd will sell stake in Solarvest Sdn Bhd for Malaysian $33.5 million.
- John Lim resigns from Jack Chia-MPH after serving as group managing director for last three years.
- John Hancock Life Assurance and Great Eastern Life launch new insurance products to take advantage of easier Central Provident Fund rules on investment.
